title: Endpoint creation + catalog browsing wireframes (model pinning flow) — draft
summary: Working draft: wireframe notes and copy options for model catalog browsing, endpoint creation flow, and model version pinning UI. Focus: reduce cognitive load when creating endpoints, make pinning explicit and reversible, surface compatibility and cost tradeoffs.
body:
Context:
- Goal: simplify 'Create Endpoint' flow for engineers and platform teams while making model selection and version pinning explicit.
- Constraints: must map to backend fields used by serving runtime (model_id, model_variant, quantization_profile, region_preference, fallback_policy).
- Audience: primary: engineers (fast path), secondary: product/platform (need clarity on SLAs/cost).

Design principles (quick):
- Progressive disclosure: show sensible defaults, reveal advanced options only when needed.
- Explicit pinning: users must opt-in to pin a model version; default is rolling to latest compatible variant.
- Cost/latency hints inline: small badges that show estimated cost-per-token and median 99th latency based on profile.
- Compatibility hints: highlight which model variants support streaming, function-calling, and quantized inference.

Notes on existing mental models:
- Users think of "model" (gpt-like name) + "version" separately; many expect pinning at creation time.
- Platform teams want easy rollback and audit trails.

Rough flow (high level):
1) Catalog browse/search (left) -> select model card -> detail pane (right) showing versions, metrics, capability matrix.
2) "Create endpoint" CTA on model detail -> endpoint creation modal (compact, stepper).
3) Step 1: Name + Route + Region (defaults).
4) Step 2: Model selection (dropdown prefilled with chosen model) + version selector (radio or dropdown with pin toggle) + variant details (quant, memory, cost badge).
5) Step 3: Capacity & SLAs (dedicated vs hosted, throughput sliders).
6) Step 4: Review & create (shows diffs vs defaults and pinning statement).

Behavior specifics: 
- Version selector: show three columns in the dropdown rows: version tag, released date, traffic compatibility (green/yellow/red), quick actions [Pin] [Set as default].
- Pinning UX: a toggle accompanied by tooltip "Pin to a specific model version to guarantee deterministic weights; unpinned endpoints will automatically receive minor patch updates." When user toggles on, show confirmation modal: "Pin to v2.3.1 — you will not receive minor patches. You can unpin later; rollback requires redeploy."
- Default (recommended) copy: "Allow minor updates (recommended) — automatically receive minor fixes while keeping the same architecture."
- If pinned, show a clear banner on endpoint page: "Pinned to model-name vX.Y.Z — changes to this endpoint will not pick up newer minor versions." Include an "Unpin" action (requires confirmation).

Wireframe considerations (visual shorthand):
- Catalog grid: compact cards with name, short description, 3 capability chips (streaming, function-calls, embeddings), median latency badge, cost badge, and an overflow menu (More -> Open details / Create endpoint / Compare).
- Model detail pane: left column: version timeline (compact vertical list), right: selected version detail with action strip (Create endpoint / Pin version / Compare).
- Endpoint modal: two-column layout on wide screens: left: form, right: cost/latency preview + compatibility matrix + example curl. On small screens collapse to single column.

Acceptance criteria (for a minimal ship):
- Users can create an endpoint from catalog detail with model and version selected.
- Pin toggle persists to endpoint metadata and is visible on endpoint overview.
- Default behavior for unpinned endpoints is documented and shown in review step.
- Cost/latency badges derive from existing model profile metrics.
- Audit fields created: pinned_by, pinned_at, pin_reason (optional free text).

Grooming notes / sizing: 
- Story: Catalog -> Create endpoint skeleton (search & CTA) – 2 SP – backend + UI hooks exist.
- Story: Version selector + pin toggle + confirmation modal – 3 SP – must write backend metadata and update endpoint schema.
- Story: Cost/latency badges + compatibility matrix – 3 SP – needs aggregation endpoint.
- Story: Unpin flow + audit trail – 2 SP.
- Story: Mobile/responsive adjustments – 1 SP.
- Blockers: model profile metrics API (PROD-821), endpoint schema migration coordination with serving-runtime.

Edge cases & risk notes: 
- Models with hundreds of micro-versions: prefer collapsible 'major version' grouping.
- Pinned major versions may require manual compatibility testing (note: flag for SRE runbook).
- Users might expect pin to freeze config only; clarify pin scope is weights (not instance type or routing).

Unresolved tradeoffs: 
- Should pin default be off (recommended) or on for enterprise tenants? Proposal: keep off globally; allow org-level policy to default to pinned endpoints (enterprise only).
- How to show cost delta for pinned vs rolling? Option: estimate relative increase in maintenance risk rather than direct cost.

Notes-to-self / rough copy fragments below for UX copy review:
- Primary CTAs: "Create endpoint" (catalog), "New endpoint" (top-level), "Add endpoint" (context).
- Pin toggle label options: 1) "Pin to version" 2) "Lock model version" 3) "Pin weights (no auto-updates)"
- Toggle helper text examples:
   • "Pin to v2.3.1 — endpoint will keep this version unless manually changed."
   • "Allow minor updates (recommended) — receive bug/quality fixes automatically."
- Confirmation modal title: "Pin endpoint to vX.Y.Z?" Body: "This will freeze the model weights for this endpoint. You can unpin later but weight updates will not be applied automatically." Buttons: [Pin and create] [Cancel]
- Review step copy: "Review endpoint configuration" subcopy: "Model: open-llama-7b (v2.3.1, pinned) • Region: us-west-2 • Throughput: 3 rps"

Quick copy alternatives for the banner when endpoint is pinned:
- Option A (concise): "Pinned to open-llama-7b v2.3.1"
- Option B (informative): "Pinned to open-llama-7b v2.3.1 — this endpoint will not automatically receive minor model updates."

Analytics/telemetry to add (minimal):
- Catalog -> create endpoint click (with model_id, version_id if selected).
- Pin toggle usage (toggled_on, toggled_off with user_id).
- Endpoint creation metadata: pinned=true/false, pin_reason text length.

Compliance / audit: ensure pin metadata written to endpoint audit log and exposed in Console > Audit > Endpoint changes.

Backchannel items (for eng):
- API change: endpoints.create needs optional pinned_version_id field and pinned_reason.
- Migration: existing endpoints with pinned flag absent default to unpinned.
- Docs: update API spec and SDK examples (js/py) to show pin usage.
wireframe_descriptions: Catalog grid: 3-up cards; each card shows name, 1-line desc, 3 capability chips, median latency badge, cost badge, overflow menu with 'Create endpoint' action.
Model detail: split pane. Left: version timeline with release dates. Right: version detail with capability matrix and 'Create endpoint' CTA. 'Pin' affordance on each version row.
Endpoint modal (stepper): Step 1 Name & Route; Step 2 Model & Version (with pin toggle); Step 3 Capacity; Step 4 Review. Right rail: cost/latency preview + example request.
Pinned endpoint overview: banner under endpoint name, small 'Unpin' action, tooltip clarifying effect. Audit entry visible in activity feed.
copy_drafts: Create endpoint — primary CTA label for catalog and detail.
Pin to version — toggle label (alt: Lock model version).
Allow minor updates (recommended) — helper text for default behavior.
This endpoint is pinned to {model} {version} — updates will not be applied automatically. Unpin to resume receiving updates.
Estimated cost: $0.003 / 1k tokens • Median latency: 120ms (99th: 420ms) — small badges used in right rail.
Confirmation modal: 'Pin endpoint to vX.Y.Z?' 'This will freeze the model weights for this endpoint. You can unpin later but automatic weight updates will be skipped.'
